questions.prompt: Select all constructs that cause Undefined Behavior in standard C. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Modifying a string literal via `char *s = "hi"; s[0] = 'H';`
Reading an uninitialized automatic local variable

questions.prompt: Match each C type qualifier to its true engineering role.

columns.label: Promises a pointer does not alias other pointers in scope, enabling optimization
Prevents compiler caching/reordering of accesses to MMIO or signal flags
Provides lock-free/synchronized atomic operations across threads (C11)

questions.prompt: Why is `volatile` NOT sufficient for synchronizing shared data between threads?

options.text: `volatile` does not guarantee atomicity or cross-CPU memory ordering barriers

questions.prompt: What does `offsetof(struct Packet, payload)` in `<stddef.h>` compute?

options.text: The byte offset of member `payload` from the start of `struct Packet`

questions.prompt: Why can `sizeof(struct S)` be larger than the sum of its member sizes?

options.text: The compiler inserts padding bytes to satisfy member alignment and trailing array alignment
C adds a hidden vtable pointer
Structs store field names at runtime
Debug symbols are embedded inside structs

questions.prompt: What is a Flexible Array Member (FAM) in C99+?

options.text: An incomplete array `T data[];` as the last member of a `struct` for single-allocation variable-length payloads

questions.prompt: Why is `printf(user_input);` a critical security vulnerability?

options.text: Format specifiers like `%s` or `%n` in `user_input` can read/write arbitrary stack memory

questions.prompt: What integer vulnerability exists in `malloc(count * sizeof(Item))` when `count` comes from untrusted input?

options.text: `count * sizeof(Item)` can overflow `size_t`, allocating a tiny buffer followed by heap overflow

questions.prompt: What does the strict aliasing rule forbid in C?

options.text: Accessing an object through a pointer of an incompatible type (other than `char *` / `unsigned char *` / `std::byte`)
Using two pointers to the same `int`

options.text: `-fsanitize=undefined` (UBSan) for signed overflow, misaligned access, and shifts
Valgrind Memcheck for leaks and uninitialized reads
`-O3 -w` to hide all warnings and checks

questions.prompt: What is wrong with `a[i] = i++;` in C?

options.text: Unsequenced modification and value computation of `i` causes Undefined Behavior

questions.prompt: What does `_Alignof(max_align_t)` represent in C11?

options.text: The strictest fundamental alignment requirement for any standard scalar type on the platform

questions.prompt: In C11 `<threads.h>` or POSIX `<pthread.h>`, why must a condition variable wait be wrapped in a `while` loop?

options.text: Spurious wakeups or another thread consuming the condition can occur before the thread resumes
It unlocks all mutexes in the process

questions.prompt: What does `static inline` in a C99/C11 header file accomplish?

options.text: Gives each translation unit its own internal definition if not inlined, avoiding multiple-definition linker errors

questions.prompt: What is the risk of `setjmp` / `longjmp` in C?

options.text: It unwinds the stack without running cleanup logic, risking leaked heap memory or locked mutexes

questions.prompt: Match each security/reliability issue in C to its mitigation.

columns.label: Use bounded `fgets` / `snprintf` with exact buffer size

questions.prompt: Why should sensitive secrets (keys/passwords) in C buffers be cleared with `explicit_bzero` or `memset_s` rather than plain `memset` before `free`?

options.text: Optimizing compilers can eliminate a dead-store `memset` right before `free` or return

questions.prompt: What does an arena (bump) allocator trade off compared to per-object `malloc`/`free`?

options.text: Fast O(1) pointer-bump allocation and bulk free of the whole arena, at the cost of not freeing individual objects early

questions.prompt: What does `va_start(ap, last)` require in a variadic function (`...`)?

options.text: At least one named parameter `last` before `...`

questions.prompt: What happens on `read()` / `write()` POSIX calls when a signal interrupts them or a socket buffer is partially full?

options.text: They always transfer the full count
They may return a short count (`< requested`) or `-1` with `errno == EINTR`

options.text: Guarantees zero runtime bugs without testing

options.text: Both are Undefined Behavior in C

questions.prompt: What does `pthread_mutex_lock` + `pthread_mutex_unlock` guarantee besides mutual exclusion?

options.text: Memory visibility (acquire/release synchronization) of shared writes between threads

questions.prompt: What causes a deadlock between two threads acquiring locks `A` and `B`?

options.text: Thread 1 holds `A` waiting for `B`, while Thread 2 holds `B` waiting for `A`

questions.prompt: Why is `realloc(p, 0)` discouraged in portable C?

options.text: Its behavior (returning `NULL` vs a minimum pointer, freeing vs not) varies across C standards and implementations

questions.prompt: Select all best practices for designing a clean C library API (header + `.c` implementation). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Return explicit error codes or status enums rather than `exit()`ing inside library code
Put all global mutable state in header files without `extern`
Hide internal struct fields behind an opaque pointer (`typedef struct Foo Foo;`) in the header

questions.prompt: What does `restrict` allow the compiler to assume in `void add(int n, int * restrict a, const int * restrict b)`?

options.text: During `add`, memory accessed via `a` does not overlap with memory accessed via `b`

questions.prompt: What is a TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) race condition in C systems programming?

options.text: Checking file permissions with `access()` and later calling `open()`, allowing an attacker to swap a symlink in between

questions.prompt: What does `strerror_r` (or `strerror_s`) solve compared to `strerror(errno)`?

options.text: It is thread-safe because it writes into a caller-provided buffer instead of a shared static buffer

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Variable Length Arrays (VLAs) in C. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Large or untrusted VLA lengths can silently overflow the stack
Their size is determined at runtime on the stack

questions.prompt: Why do C projects often wrap `malloc` or file handles with `goto cleanup;` in functions with multiple resources?

options.text: To centralize deterministic resource cleanup in reverse acquisition order without duplicating `free`/`fclose` at every error return
